8 minutes read

Offing privacy

Offing analyzes software repositories on the user's computer. The Codex and Claude plugins start a local stdio MCP server and do not send repository contents to an Offing-operated service. Offing does not require an Offing account, collect analytics, use advertising identifiers, or sell personal data.

The local tools read supported manifests, lockfiles, workflow files, runtime-version files, and relevant source excerpts from the repository path the user authorizes. Results can contain file paths and short source excerpts. The host application receives those results, so its privacy policy and the user's workspace settings also apply.

The plugin launches the exact published offing npm version recorded in its manifest. The package manager may contact the configured npm registry to obtain that package. Lifecycle evidence links are returned as references; Offing does not open them automatically.

Lifecycle data channel

Scans use no network. The one exception is offing data update, which you run yourself to fetch newer lifecycle rules between releases. Rules ship inside each release; that command downloads a public release list and two public files (the signed bundle and its signature) from the project's GitHub releases, verifies the Sigstore signature offline against a trusted root that ships in the package, and activates the new rules only after verification succeeds. If verification fails, Offing keeps the rules bundled with the installed release and reports why. Pinning with --data-version or OFFING_DATA_VERSION makes CI use an exact verified bundle (or bundled). It sends nothing about you or your repository. See Lifecycle data.

Command and surface access

Supply-chain scanners correctly report that the published package can read files, read environment variables, spawn processes (including git), and reach the network. Those capabilities are real; they are not used by every command. This table is the contract for what each surface actually does. "Scan path" means the repository (or paths) you pass on the command line or to a tool. Nothing here uploads repository contents to an Offing service.

Surface / command Filesystem Environment Child process Network
CLI scan, forecast, status-card, explain, context, renovate-preset, dependabot-config Reads the scan path (manifests, lockfiles, workflows, source). Optional writes only when you ask: --write-status → OFFING_STATUS.md; --baseline reads a baseline file. status-card, renovate-preset, and dependabot-config print to stdout only OFFING_DATA_VERSION (pin bundled/cached rules); OFFING_DATA_DIR / XDG_CACHE_HOME / HOME for cached data; --interactive uses VISUAL or EDITOR to open a finding --interactive may spawn your editor. No git, no package manager None
CLI lookup, check None for the rules themselves (package or local data cache). check takes a Package URL; lookup takes a product name Same data-pin and cache variables as scan; optional OFFING_USAGE_LOG appends one local line for check None None
CLI badge --shields reads the scan path and prints Shields endpoint JSON. --snippet prints README markup only None beyond process defaults for --snippet; data-pin variables when --shields scans Without --repo, --snippet may run local git remote get-url origin (no remotes fetched) None (image URLs in the markup are references; Offing does not fetch them)
CLI usage Reads the local usage-log file when logging was enabled OFFING_USAGE_LOG, or --file None None
CLI baseline Reads the scan path; writes .offing-baseline.json (or --output) Same data-pin and cache variables as scan None None
CLI report-issue Reads the scan path and a few lines of the declaring file; optional --output write Same data-pin and cache variables as scan None None (prints Markdown; never opens an issue)
CLI rollup Reads the saved report JSON files you name (and optional --owners file) None beyond process defaults None None
CLI inventory Reads only the export files named on the command line and the bundled or cached lifecycle data; no cloud or cluster API EBB_DATA_DIR / cache home variables for lifecycle data None None
CLI sbom enrich, export Reads the SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX 2.3) or bundled/cached lifecycle data; prints enriched JSON or CLE snapshots to stdout; leaves the input unchanged Data-pin and cache variables as above None None
CLI capabilities, completions, --help, --version None (packaged constants / scripts) None None None
CLI data status Reads the local data cache and bundled rules EBB_DATA_DIR / cache home variables None None
CLI data update Writes verified bundles under the local data cache EBB_DATA_URL (optional mirror); HTTP(S)_PROXY / http(s)_proxy; cache home variables. May relaunch Node with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY when a proxy is set May re-exec the same Node process so proxy env is honored Yes — public GitHub release list plus the signed bundle and signature only. Sends no repository data
CLI diff Reads git objects into a temp directory, then scans them; leaves the working tree alone Same data-pin and cache variables as scan Runs local git archive and tar (no remotes) None
CLI doctor Reads the install layout and, for the path argument, local project markers Detects CI via GITHUB_ACTIONS / GITLAB_CI and related workspace variables With --system, runs fixed version commands (node, python3, go, …) with a short timeout None
CLI guard None for the check itself Same as check for the preflight After a passing check, spawns the package manager you named (npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, …) with your arguments Only whatever that package manager does after Offing exits the check
CLI fix Reads the scan path. Default: prints patches to stdout (no write). --branch: applies and commits on a new local branch Same data-pin and cache variables as scan --branch runs local git (checkout, apply, add, commit); never push None
CLI init --agents, setup Reads/writes agent instruction files in the scan path (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, host rule files, …) None beyond process defaults None None
CLI init (guided, no flags) Reads the CI provider and agent markers in the scan path; writes .github/workflows/offing.yml, .git/hooks/pre-push, and agent files (after confirmation unless --yes) None beyond process defaults Runs git rev-parse to locate hooks None
CLI init --hooks Reads/writes .git/hooks/pre-push (or the path git reports) None beyond process defaults Runs git rev-parse to locate hooks None
CLI init --personal Writes ~/.config/offing/ (or XDG_CONFIG_HOME) config and a global pre-push hook HOME / USERPROFILE, XDG_CONFIG_HOME Runs git config --global core.hooksPath (after confirmation unless --yes) None
CLI watch Reads registered projects (same as scan); reads/writes watch.json under the personal config directory HOME / XDG_CONFIG_HOME for state location; same data-pin variables when scanning None None
CLI new-detector, new-rule, rules lint, rules test Contributor checkout only: scaffolds detector or rule fixtures, or reads registry fixtures under the repo None None None
CLI mcp / offing mcp Same reads as the tools below; no repository writes Optional OFFING_USAGE_LOG for check_dependency; data-pin and cache variables None (stdio only; no shell for migrations) None
MCP tools (scan_repository, list_deprecations, explain_deprecation, create_migration_context, verify_migration, check_dependency) Read the authorized repository path (except check_dependency, which reads no repository). Session findings stay in memory Same as MCP process above None — verify_migration returns suggested commands and does not run them None
offing lsp Reads/scans workspace folders; may write open buffer text into a private temp directory for analysis None beyond process defaults None None (stdio language server)
GitHub Action Reads path (default workspace); may write report/SARIF/badge under RUNNER_TEMP when upload inputs are on; reads GITHUB_EVENT_PATH for PR metadata Action inputs as INPUT_*, plus GITHUB_WORKSPACE, GITHUB_OUTPUT, GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_API_URL, RUNNER_TEMP, and INPUT_GITHUB-TOKEN when commenting None from Offing itself Only when pr-comment: true: GitHub API upsert of one PR comment after the scan. The scan itself uses no network
GitLab CI/CD component Reads the checked-out path; writes the JSON report and Code Quality report as job artifacts Component inputs and standard GitLab CI variables; no access token required None from Offing itself (npx runs the pinned package) None for the scan. Before the scan, the runner may pull the job image and npx may fetch the pinned package from the configured npm registry. No GitLab API call; see GitLab
Agent Skill / Codex & Claude plugins No direct I/O: they launch the local MCP server or tell the host to run CLI commands under the host's permission model Host may set env when spawning MCP/CLI Host may spawn npx / Node to start MCP Package install may hit the npm registry; analysis stays local

Notes that apply across rows:

  • Detectors never call the network and never execute repository code. Repository contents are parsed as data.
  • Evidence URLs in findings are references only; Offing does not open them.
  • Maintainer-only scripts under tools/ (importers, source checks, adoption metrics) can use the network and optional GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN. They are not part of the published CLI scan path and are not in the table above.
  • Socket and similar scanners flag the capability (filesystem, env, child process, URL strings) because the code exists in the tarball. Use this table to see which command exercises which capability.

Local usage log

By default Offing records nothing about what you or an agent checked. If you set OFFING_USAGE_LOG=1 (or to a file path), each offing check and each check_dependency call appends one line to a file on your machine: the time, the package URL and version checked, the result, its severity, and the matching rule IDs. It records no repository path, file content, user name, or prompt. offing usage reads that file and prints how many checks ran and which packages were flagged as affected (what the guardrail told an agent to avoid; Offing cannot itself stop an edit). Nothing in this log is sent anywhere: Offing has no code that uploads it, and the summary command reads only the local file. Delete the file to erase it; unset the variable to stop recording. Because the file lives on disk, anything that can read your files can read it.

Offing's tools do not edit repository files, execute suggested migration commands, open a network listener, or request credentials — except the explicit write and process rows in the table above (baseline, --write-status, init / setup, fix --branch, guard's package manager, and similar). Users can disable or remove the plugin at any time. Questions can be reported through GitHub Issues.
